text: We evaluated weak-to-strong generalization with an auxiliary confidence loss on the strong student (aux_loss_weight 0.5), using pythia-410m as the weak supervisor and llama-3.1-8b as the strong student, across 4 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.51 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling performance was 0.91. Training the strong student on weak labels with the auxiliary loss yielded a transfer accuracy of 0.64 (SE 0.01) and a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.32 (SE 0.03), compared with a baseline PGR of 0.15. The gap between the measured PGR and the baseline exceeds twice the reported standard error, so the auxiliary loss appears to recover more of the weak-to-strong gap than the baseline under this setup. Two caveats temper the reading: only 4 seeds were run, which limits how firmly the effect size can be pinned down, and no standard error is reported for the baseline PGR, so the comparison rests on the treatment's variance alone.
